parameters.title: Regression modeling of indicators from different covariates
parameters.label: Regression modeling of indicators from spectra and/or covariates with an array of machine learning regressors: ols (ordinary least squares), theil_sen (Theil-Sen robust regressor), huber (Huber robust regressor), knn (k-nearest neighbours), dectree (decision tree), randfor (random forest), svr (support vector regressor), mlp (multi-layer perceptron), cubist (rule-based) and plsr (partial least squares).

parameter.hint: The root fp of the project
The dataframe to use as input, raw = original spectra, previous = the latest saved parquet file(s), or state the name of the parquet file with spectra derived from earlier step(s) to use as input.
Comma separated list of the indicators to evaluate.

Covariates used next to the spectra: empty = spectra only, all = every covariate of the (compiled) dataset, or the covariate names. Numeric covariates are used as they are, nominal (class) covariates are one-hot encoded. Samples missing a covariate are skipped, also when predicting.

Pool the classes of nominal covariates into groups before encoding: [{"covariate": "soil texture usda", "groups": [["sand", "loamy sand"], ["loam", "silt loam"], ...]}]. Every class in the data must be placed in a group. Predefined groupings are separate covariates, e.g. soil texture usda major group. Optional "other": "exclude" leaves the samples of classes not in any group out (not modelled, not predicted); "other": "<name>" pools them into one group.
Regressors to apply: ols, theil_sen, huber, knn, dectree, randfor, svr, mlp, cubist, plsr.
Regressor hyper-parameters: default (the standard regressor set), none (scikit-learn defaults), a parameter set name[@version] or a JSON file path relative to the project root.
whether or not to apply regression modeling using a train- test division of the source data (dataframe)
whether or not to apply regression modeling using a train- test division of the source data (dataframe)
whether or not to apply regression modeling using a k-fold approach

Transformation of the indicator(s) before modeling: none, default (the standard set), a parameter set name[@version] or a JSON file path relative to the project root. Fitted on the training samples; predictions are returned in the native unit.
Z-score standardisation of the indicator(s) before modeling: none, default (the standard set), a parameter set name[@version] or a JSON file path relative to the project root.

Refit the preprocessing chain of the input dataframe (from its companion JSON) on the training samples inside the model pipeline, starting from the unprocessed source parquet. false = train on the preprocessed dataframe as is (preprocessing fitted on all samples, optimistic test metrics).
Folder for the saved models (.joblib + .manifest.json), relative to the project root. Empty = <project_root_fp>/models.
number of folds for the k-fold approach (used when kfold is true)
The symbolisation of indicators, if not set to default you have to give a relative or abolute path
The symbolisation of regressors, if not set to default you have to give a relative or abolute path
Maximum number of features to show in importance/permutation bar plots. 0 = show all. Y-axis labels are suppressed when showing more than 40 features.
Show observed vs predicted plot on screen or not.
Save observed vs predicted plot to file or not.
Show permutation importance plot on screen or not.
Save permutation importance plot to file or not.
Show feature importance plot on screen or not.
Save feature importance plot to file or not.

How the shown plots are arranged: default (picked from what is shown, the modes and the number of indicators/regressors), a preset (scatter-1, scatter-2, scatter-3, scatter-4, scatter-tt-kf, importance), a custom plot_layout parameter set, a JSON file (relative or absolute path), or none (one figure per plot, as before). Saved plots are always single figures.
Also save the grid figures of plot_layout, under plot/<dataframe>_grid/.

Only map the feature and permutation importance: the regressors are fitted (train/test: on the training samples, permutation on the test samples; kfold: on all samples), but no scatter, metrics, k-fold predictions or models are made or saved.
